clue.text: Look for quiet in a school

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside the second

blocks.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
a school of thought or belief, a sect

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to look for some peace and quiet inside a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' as a noun: the look of a building is its aspect. A school of thought is a sect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is how something appears to the eye, its outward appearance or expression.

clue.text: Judges a rider's about to crack up

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
a rider is an added note, a postscript, PS
to crack someone up is to speak very highly of them

explanation.surface: Panel members rate how a jockey falls apart under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack up' looks like a breakdown; it also means to praise, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'. PS goes about it: A + P(PRAISE)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who appraises assesses the value or quality of something, as a judge does.

clue.text: One goes through new recipe -- it's about right

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so these letters take a fresh order
it's about means it goes around, enclosing what follows

blocks.note: the letters of recipe in a new order
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cook works through a new recipe and finds it about right.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercer is something or someone that makes a hole by passing through a thing.

clue.text: Private communication of faith

blocks.note: first meaning: a secret told to someone trusted
second meaning: trust or belief in someone

explanation.surface: A private message expressing someone's religious belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence is a secret shared in trust, and the word also means firm trust or belief in someone.

clue.text: Gather a number on the roadside

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
a verge is the grass strip along the edge of a road

explanation.surface: A crowd assembles at the edge of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is often a Roman numeral: here C. In Britain the verge is the grassy strip at the side of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to come together at one point, as people do when they assemble.

clue.text: Work iron and gold for a taskmaster

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
to iron clothes is to press them
or is gold in heraldry; and simply joins

explanation.surface: A harsh boss orders a smith to work iron and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work iron' reads like smithing; all three words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor treats people harshly and cruelly, like a demanding master driving workers.

clue.text: To struggle without money is awful

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: to vie is to compete, struggle
L for pound, libra, money

explanation.surface: Being broke and fighting to get by is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside, so VIE wraps L.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile means extremely unpleasant or bad, much like dreadful.

clue.text: Storm about a member standing up

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: to storm is to rage and rant
taken as written
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone rages about an MP who rises to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing up' sounds like an MP rising; it is a heraldry term for a beast reared on its hind legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a rampant lion is shown rearing on its hind legs, upright with forepaws raised.

clue.text: The man turned in here in readiness

definitions.note: a man's name standing for the man named

indicators.note: the letters sit in the words that follow, across their breaks
turned round means read from end to start

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of here, all of in, and the start of readiness

explanation.surface: A man has gone to bed here, ready for the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned in' looks like going to bed; split it: turned is reversal, in is the hidden signal. ERNIE is also Britain's Premium Bond number-drawing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's first name, a short form of Ernest, so it can stand for a particular man.

clue.text: Centre of front row for a once revered figure

indicators.note: the centre of a word is the single letter in its middle

blocks.note: the middle letter of front
a row is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: A seat in the middle of the front row is kept for a once-honoured celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front row' reads as one phrase; the two words do separate jobs, and row rhymes with cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin was chief god of Norse mythology, worshipped by Vikings and no longer venerated.

clue.text: Prepared for flight

blocks.note: surface reading: got ready to run away, or packed for a plane journey
setter's reading: what a bird did to its feathers before flying off

explanation.surface: A fugitive or a traveller has got everything ready to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests escape or air travel; the setter means a bird tidying its plumage before taking wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds smooth and arrange their feathers with the beak, which keeps the plumage in order for flying.

clue.text: Having influence, fellow gets luxurious transport

blocks.note: pull is influence, as in having pull with someone
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A well-connected man is rewarded with a smart ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pullman is a comfortable railway carriage with superior seating and service, named after its American designer.

clue.text: He wants to dispose of the lot!

definitions.text: He wants to dispose of the lot!

blocks.clueFragment: He wants to dispose of the lot!
blocks.note: surface reading: someone keen to get rid of everything at once

blocks.clueFragment: He wants to dispose of the lot!
blocks.note: setter's reading: a lot is an item for sale in a saleroom, and this man sells each one to the highest bidder

explanation.surface: A man clearing out wants rid of every last thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lot' reads as 'everything', but a lot is a numbered item at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running a sale by bidding sells each lot, knocking it down with a hammer to whoever bids most.

clue.text: The head's cloak

blocks.note: first meaning: a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea
second meaning: a sleeveless garment worn over the shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a headteacher's gown; 'head' is a headland, and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is both a promontory jutting into the sea and a short sleeveless outer garment hung from the shoulders.

clue.text: The manicurist?

blocks.note: surface reading: the person who does your nails
setter's reading: a maid who attends to hands, a hand-maid; really a female servant

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as hand + maiden: a girl who looks after hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaiden is a female personal attendant or servant, and one who tends hands could be called one jokingly.

clue.text: There's too much foam - drawback, that

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun: a surfeit is a case of there being too much

blocks.note: surf is the foam of breaking waves
split as draw + back: a drawn match is a tie, and back has it run the other way

explanation.surface: Too much froth on a pint is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one word meaning a snag; split it into draw + back.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, an oversupply of something beyond what is wanted.

clue.text: Exciting article about running water

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: an article is a thing, an item
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A gripping magazine piece about rivers and streams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' wants to be a, an or the; here it is an item, a thing. TH(RILL)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling means causing a sudden rush of excitement and pleasure.

clue.text: Opener to lead the King

blocks.note: to lead off is to start
ER, Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A batsman opening the innings is to go in ahead of the King.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is more often the Queen; here it stands for Edward Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter opens a meal, or is the person who opens a race by giving the signal.

clue.text: A variety of stones are used in rings

indicators.note: a variety offers different forms, so these letters appear in another order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Jewellers set various gems in rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like jewellery, which suits stones; it is the verb, to ring out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resonates echoes with a deep, sustained sound, as a bell does when it rings.

clue.text: Cider's a way-out drink!

indicators.note: something way-out is wild and eccentric, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone declares cider a really far-out drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Drawing of an Indian city with dull frame

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: dim means dull, not bright
Agra, the city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A sketch of an Indian city mounted in a drab frame.
explanation.walkthrough: DIM frames AGRA: DI(AGRA)M.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawing showing the parts or workings of something.

clue.text: Set right about clothes

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
dress is clothing

explanation.surface: Someone corrects an error concerning what people wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy or correct it, putting the matter back in order.

clue.text: Record one's poem or chapter

blocks.note: an EP, extended-play record
one is I, and 's is is
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: Someone records their own poem or a chapter of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment or section of a series or story, much like a chapter.

clue.text: To the doctor an indication of distress

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient shows the doctor a symptom of being unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a low mournful sound of pain or unhappiness, or a complaint.

clue.text: An operatic heroine many imitate

blocks.note: Mimi, the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of singers copy a famous operatic heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives a Roman numeral, here C for a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to copy someone's voice or manner, often to amuse.

clue.text: Change the blend of tea on trial

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A tea company tries out a new blend before switching.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an alteration is a modification or adjustment that makes something different.

clue.text: Effective uprising in the Mediterranean

definitions.note: a place description standing for the island it describes

indicators.note: rising up in a down entry means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: able means capable, effective

explanation.surface: A successful revolt breaks out somewhere around the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is an Italian island off Tuscany, famous as Napoleon's place of exile.

clue.text: Type of sanctimonious accountant

blocks.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
CA, chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A kind of self-righteous bookkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like 'kind'; it is printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a size of printing type, about twelve points, and a typewriter typeface.

clue.text: In short, the skill needed to make a cocktail

indicators.note: one thing in another means it is placed inside the second

blocks.note: mini means short, as in a miniskirt
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Briefly put, some craft is required to mix a good cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' looks like 'briefly'; split it, and short is the miniskirt sense of mini.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and dry vermouth, usually served with an olive.

clue.text: Letters for the patient?

blocks.note: surface reading: mail delivered to someone in hospital
setter's reading: the patient lies in bed; really an upright at a corner of a bed

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the mail for a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, bed + post, and it means mail for the bedridden.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing named is an upright at one corner of a bed frame, which split in two also means mail delivered to a bedridden person.

clue.text: Drive a camping convertible

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone takes a convertible car out on a camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convertible' looks like a car, which suits 'Drive'; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is an organised effort to achieve something, such as a fundraising or election push.

clue.text: This French place causes some offence

blocks.note: first meaning: a city on the Loire in western France
second meaning: makes someone cross

explanation.surface: A French town manages to put people's backs up.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a historic city in the Loire valley, and the English verb means makes someone irritated or annoyed.
